question: Should five consecutive syntactically malformed Google Meet `pullAudio` chunks terminate the active audio bridge under the existing input-failure cutoff?
rationale: Source and proof establish that the implementation is coherent, but only the Google Meet owner can confirm whether malformed producer data should share the same terminal availability policy as repeated invocation failures.

options.title: Keep bounded shutdown
options.body: Treat malformed pulled audio as an input failure, recover after valid data, and stop after five consecutive malformed chunks to avoid forwarding garbage or looping indefinitely.

options.title: Separate malformed-data handling
options.body: Drop malformed chunks without using the terminal invoke-failure counter, with a separately defined health or shutdown policy and matching proof.

recommendation.title: Keep bounded shutdown
recommendation.body: Treat malformed pulled audio as an input failure, recover after valid data, and stop after five consecutive malformed chunks to avoid forwarding garbage or looping indefinitely.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows this person merged both the original plugin and the lifecycle change that introduced the cutoff being extended.
